intent.goal: Close #441/#443/#444 by naming, in runtime/mission-chaining.md, the terminal a chain parks at when a human promotion is owed and what resumes it; the one artifact the mandated deferral carry rides in; and what re-derivability means for a leg whose target has no remote. Round 2 answers review round 1's NO-GO on all three axes: correct the promotion boundary to BASE->DEFAULT, require commit-preserving reconstruction, bind the contract test to obligations rather than vocabulary, re-record the negative control through evidence-run.py, make the exemplar's adoption explicit, and re-verify on the now-green BASE.
intent.ruled_out: Touching verify.py or evidence-manifest.md (#442's cross-repo evidence-root gap is the separate U-442 unit); adding PARKED-AT-PROMOTION to ledger-contract.md's terminal table or to any mission guide (would change another policy, which the spec's stop rule forbids); a new runtime policy file for chain parking (the three gaps are clauses of an existing contract, not a new one); a standalone tests/test_mission_chaining.py (test_architecture.py already owns this file's docs-contract seam, and test_chain_terminals_are_decidable_by_rule sits beside the new test). Round 2 additionally ruled out: rewriting docs/reports/chaining-2026-09-16/handoff-log.md or leg1/RESTORE.md (the spec forbids editing the historical artifact — F-5 fixes the CITING text instead); editing gate-classification.md or merge-serialization.md to match the new wording (the shared doctrine was already right; this policy was the one that diverged); a semantic Markdown parser for the contract test (the reviewers asked for specific assertions, not a general oracle).
intent.why: The gaps are consequences the policy never drew, not missing vocabulary — so the fix has to read as a rule a coordinator can follow at 3am, and the test has to bind each property to ONE bullet. Asserting the tokens file-wide would have stayed green against a doc that sprinkled them across unrelated prose. PARKED-AT-PROMOTION is deliberately typed as a CHAIN state, not a mission terminal, because the existing degradation-marker rule classifies TERMINALS and a promotion park is the normal outcome of a CLEAN leg — typing it as a terminal would have made every healthy chain look degraded. The round-1 test failed the way documentation contracts usually fail: it pinned the words that NAME a rule and not the words that give it FORCE, so 'neither is a precondition', 'two optional examples' and 'a list of commit SHAs is sufficient' all stayed green. Each assertion now quotes the obligation clause itself, and bullets are whitespace-normalised first so a reflow cannot read as a doctrine change (S3).
